newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Soaring Thai power demand to fuel use of copper.
newsitem.headline: Soaring Thai power demand to fuel use of copper.

text.p: The strong expansion in Thai electricity consumption should boost the demand for base metals such as copper in the country, the president and chief executive officer of Bangkok Cable Co Ltd said on Tuesday.
Sompong Nakornsri said at a copper conference in Singapore that power consumption for the past 10 years has grown at an average rate of 12 percent a year in Thailand.
"The government would have to spend more than 100 billion baht annually to build power plants to meet the demand," Sompong said.
Total consumption of cable products ranging from low voltage cable to magnet or enamel wire soared to 137,000 tonnes in 1996 from 84,000 tonnes in 1991, Sompong said.
Low voltage cable consumption has eased because of the virtual collapse of the property market in Thailand.

But any slack from construction should easily be filled by an increase in automotive demand, especially with the decision by U.S. giant General Motors to build a huge assembly plant in Thailand, the Bangkok Cable Co official said.
The increasing affluence of the Thai middle class will also lead to increased spending on airconditioning units and cars which are heavy users of cables containing copper, he added.
